Description: explicit — omitted glyphs field, text renders in wrong font
prompt: My MapLibre GL JS stylesheet has no `glyphs` property set at all, and my symbol layers have `text-font` set to a font name. Text labels are showing up, but in a generic font, not the one I specified. Is this a bug I need to fix, or expected behavior? What's actually happening?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### Short answer No – it’s **expected** behaviour. When a style **does not have a `glyphs` URL**, MapLibre GL JS falls back to its **local-font mode** (added in v5.11). Every `text-font` name is treated exactly like a CSS `font-family` list: 1. The browser tries to find a **system font** with that name. 2. If you have supplied a **web-font** (via `@font-face` or `map.setFontFaces()`), it will be used. 3. If the name can’t be resolved, the browser falls back to its generic default (usually “sans-serif”), which is what you’re seeing. So the map isn’t “broken”; it’s simply rendering with whatever font the browser could locate. --- ## What’s really happening under the hood | Step | What MapLibre does | Why it matters for you | |------|-------------------|------------------------| | **Style parsing** | No `glyphs` field → *local-fonts mode* is activated. | No glyph-PBF requests are ever made. | | **Layer evaluation** | `text-font: ["My Fancy Font"]` is read as a CSS font-family list. | The name must match a font the browser can resolve. | | **Font resolution** | 1️⃣ Look for a **system font** named *My Fancy Font*.
2️⃣ If you called `map.setFontFaces({ "My Fancy Font": [{url:"…"}] })` (or declared the same mapping in the style’s `font-faces` property), the browser will download that file and use it.
3️⃣ If neither step succeeds, the browser falls back to its generic family (`sans-serif`, `serif`, etc.). | The generic font you see is the browser’s fallback. | | **Rendering** | Glyphs are generated on-the-fly with **TinySDF** (an SDF rasterizer) from the resolved font. | No glyph-PBFs, no network errors, but the visual result depends on the actual font used. | > **Key point:** The `glyphs` URL is *not* required for any text to appear. It is only needed when you want to serve pre-computed SDF glyph PBFs (the classic Mapbox-style approach) or when you need the same style to work on older MapLibre GL JS versions or on MapLibre Native (which still expects a `glyphs` URL). --- ## Why you’re seeing a “generic” font 1. **The font isn’t installed on the client OS** – e.g., “My Fancy Font” is a custom corporate font that only exists on your design workstation. 2. **You haven’t loaded it as a web-font** – no `@font-face` rule, no `font-faces` entry, and you didn’t call `map.setFontFaces()`. 3. **The name you wrote in `text-font` does not exactly match the font’s internal name** – CSS is case-sensitive for the family name you declare in `@font-face`. 4. **CORS / fetch failure** – if you did declare a `font-faces` entry but the URL can’t be fetched (blocked by CORS, 404, etc.), the browser discards it and falls back. All of these result in the browser’s generic fallback being used, which is why the labels look “plain”. --- ## How to get the exact font you want ### 1. Load the font as a web-font (recommended) ```css /* In your page’s CSS */ @font-face { font-family: "My Fancy Font"; src: url("https://example.com/fonts/MyFancyFont.woff2") format("woff2"); font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; } ``` or, if you prefer to keep the mapping inside the style JSON: ```json { "font-faces": { "My Fancy Font": [ { "url": "https://example.com/fonts/MyFancyFont.woff2" } ] } } ``` Then, after the map is created (or before, if you use the JSON form), you can also call: ```js map.setFontFaces({ "My Fancy Font": [ { url: "https://example.com/fonts/MyFancyFont.woff2" } ] }); ``` **Result:** `text-font: ["My Fancy Font"]` will now resolve to the exact font you supplied, and TinySDF will rasterise that font for every label. ### 2. Use a system-installed font If the font is already installed on every target device (e.g., “Arial”, “Helvetica”, “Noto Sans”), just make sure the name you write in `text-font` matches the system name exactly. No extra work is needed. ### 3. Serve glyph PBFs instead (only if you need them) If you want to support older GL JS versions or MapLibre Native, add a `glyphs` URL that points at a glyph server (e.g., `https://mytileserver.com/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`). Then: ```json { "glyphs": "https://mytileserver.com/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", "layers": [ { "id": "place-labels", "type": "symbol", "layout": { "text-field": "{name}", "text-font": ["My Fancy Font"] } } ] } ``` Now the map will request the pre-computed SDF glyphs instead of generating them locally. This is **optional** for modern GL JS but required for native clients. ### 4. Verify the name matches the font-face entry The name used in `text-font` **must** be identical to the key you use in `font-faces` or the `font-family` you declare in CSS. Example of a mismatch: ```json "text-font": ["My Fancy Font"] // <-- expects exactly this string ``` ```json "font-faces": { "MyFancyFont": [ // <-- missing space → mismatch { "url": "..." } ] } ``` Fix the typo and the font will be found. --- ## Quick checklist for “generic font” problems | ✅ | Action | |---|--------| | **1** | Confirm the `glyphs` property is **absent** (or you deliberately omitted it). | | **2** | Verify the font you want is either (a) installed on the OS **or** (b) served as a web-font. | | **3** | If using a web-font, make sure the `font-family` name in `@font-face` **exactly** matches the string in `text-font`. | | **4** | If you prefer the style-JSON way, add a matching entry under `font-faces` (or call `map.setFontFaces()`). | | **5** | Check the network console for any 404 / CORS errors on the font file URL. | | **6** | If you need the style to work on older GL JS or on MapLibre Native, add a proper `glyphs` URL instead of relying on local-font mode. | --- ## TL;DR for your situation - **What you see is normal**: without a `glyphs` URL, MapLibre falls back to the browser’s font-resolution mechanism. - **Why you get a generic font**: the browser can’t find a font that matches the name you gave. - **Fix**: load the desired font as a web-font (via `@font-face`, `font-faces`, or `map.setFontFaces()`), or install it on the client OS. If you need the classic glyph-PBF path (e.g., for older GL JS or native), add a `glyphs` URL that serves the appropriate PBFs. Once the font is correctly reachable, the labels will render in the exact typeface you specified. No bug to file—just a matter of supplying the font the browser can actually use.
